parsedVerdict.reasoning: The module is broadly cohesive. in-memory-repositories.ts implements the domain repository interfaces, order-controller.ts is the HTTP adapter over OrderService, and server.ts is the composition root. None of them bypasses the repository or service abstractions. However, order-controller.ts keeps its own list of valid order states (STATES) and validates input against it in requiredState(). That list repeats a domain invariant that the domain's OrderState type already defines. The readonly OrderState[] annotation only checks that each listed value is a real state, not that every state is listed. So if a state is added to or renamed in OrderState, the controller will reject it without any compiler error. The controller also hard-codes the states that get a direct transition route ("paid", "packed", "shipped", "delivered"), which repeats state-machine knowledge that belongs in the domain. src/domain/order.ts was not provided, so it is unconfirmed whether the domain already exports a states constant the controller could reuse. Confidence is moderate because the module otherwise holds together well.
